reviews.text:
The atmosphere and seating of this place are quite authentic. But unfortunately that is where the pleasant experience really ends.

We ordered butter chicken, dal makhni and breads for main course. The server (who had also taken the order) brought malai kofta instead of butter chicken. Despite the order being very clearly communicated to her.

This could have been accepted as an honest mistake. But when asked to take it back, this lady staff started arguing in a loud voice that it was somehow our mistake. This is simply not acceptable.

One goes to a restaurant to have a good time. Not to be spoken rudely to in front of your family. This individual clearly does not do her job properly. And misbehaves when she is asked for the correct order.

The food barely makes the cut. The items we ordered - Dahi papdi, tandoori roti, butter naan, butter chicken and dal makhni - were all just about average. These are all essentials of any Punjabi restaurant and one expects better.

This restaurant can be avoided. I feel for the promoters here - a lot of thought, effort and capital have clearly gone into running this place. But it’s just not being run properly.

reviews.text:
I found myself back at this restaurant thanks to my friends’ demands, and here’s my updated take on the experience!
This time, I tried the chicken tandoor, and it was absolutely delicious—highly recommended! The chicken tikka with pepper was also fantastic, with a lovely smoky flavour. We ordered it twice because we weren’t quite happy with just one serving 😜
For the main course, we enjoyed butter naan and butter chicken, both of which were excellent.
The lassi was even better than before, with a lovely addition of kesar and badam.
The seating is comfy and cosy, with a Punjabi feel all around.
I’d definitely recommend the lassi and chicken tikka (pepper) as my top dishes.
